cards.text: Friend, this is the prophet Jeremiah telling us what the LORD had him do. It starts with an errand: the LORD tells him to go buy a linen loincloth and put it around his waist. Not a scroll, not a sword, a LOINCLOTH.

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah to buy a linen loincloth and wear it, but not to let it touch ___.

answers.text: water
fire
oil

cards.question: Strange orders, but Jeremiah buys the loincloth and puts it around his waist, just as the LORD said.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah a second time: take the loincloth you're wearing and go at once to Perath. At ONCE, friend, no "let me just finish this batch first."

cards.question: Jeremiah is headed to Perath with the loincloth the LORD told him to buy. What is he supposed to do with it there?

answers.text: Hide it in a crack in the rocks
Wash it and leave it to dry
Hand it over to a priest

cards.text: Jeremiah hides it at Perath as the LORD commanded, and many days later the LORD sends him back to get it. Hidden in the dark for days, waiting on somebody to remember you're there… I have NO idea what that's like.

cards.question: After many days hidden in the rocks at Perath, Jeremiah digs up the loincloth. What shape is it in?

answers.text: Ruined and of no use at all
Clean as the day he bought it
Faded but still fine to wear

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes, and now we find out what that loincloth was all about. Jeremiah's been walking around wearing a message this WHOLE time.

cards.question: The LORD says He will ruin something in the same way the loincloth was ruined. What is it?

answers.text: The pride of Judah and Jerusalem
The harvest of Judah and Jerusalem
The walls of Judah and Jerusalem

cards.text: The LORD says who He means: evil people who follow the stubbornness of their own hearts. They'll be like that loincloth, of no use at all.

cards.question: Besides following their own stubborn hearts, these people go after other ___ to serve and worship them.

answers.text: gods
nations
kings

cards.text: Then the LORD explains the picture. Just as a loincloth clings to a man's waist, He made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to Him.

cards.question: The LORD made Israel and Judah cling to Him the way a loincloth clings to a man's waist. Why?

answers.text: To be His people for His glory
To keep them safe from every war
To make them richer than the nations

cards.question: The house of Israel and the house of Judah listened to the LORD.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Next the LORD gives Jeremiah a saying to deliver. This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Every wineskin shall be filled with wine.'

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the people that every wineskin shall be filled with wine. How do they answer him?

answers.text: We surely know that already
Then bring us the wine now
Our wineskins are all empty

cards.text: That's like me walking into my own bakery and announcing, "Ovens get HOT." But the LORD's saying has a twist: He's going to fill everyone who lives in this land with drunkenness.

cards.question: The LORD says the kings who sit on David's throne and the priests will be spared from this drunkenness.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line in the whole passage. The LORD says He will smash them against one another, fathers and sons alike.

cards.question: The LORD says He will smash the people of the land against one another. What does He say about holding back?

answers.text: No mercy or pity will stop Him
He will spare all the prophets
He will wait one more year

findings.problem: "Jeremiah's been walking around wearing a message this WHOLE time" is presented as fact, but the text shows otherwise. Jeremiah wore the loincloth (13:2), then hid it at Perath for many days (13:5-6) and dug it up ruined (13:7). He wasn't wearing it the whole time, and the text never says he walked around in it.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says "these people" without saying who they are, the evil people of Judah and Jerusalem (13:9-10). It points back to a story card that is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question tells 13:12 as an event: Jeremiah tells the people and they answer. In the text, the LORD is instructing Jeremiah what to say, and the people's reply is something the LORD says will happen ("when they reply"). The text doesn't narrate Jeremiah delivering the saying or the people answering. The question should frame it as what the LORD says they will reply.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The story card says the LORD will fill "everyone who lives in this land" with drunkenness. That gives away card 18, which asks whether the kings and priests will be spared. The answer is False, and "everyone" already rules out True.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Spared from this drunkenness" points back to card 17 with "this" and doesn't say what the drunkenness is: the LORD filling all who live in the land with it (13:13).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. Of 11 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice, 3 are true or false and only 2 are fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
